title: Constants
description: Shared compile-time constants. Single source of truth for both the TypeScript frontend (src) and the Rust backend (src-tauri). Edit values.json; never edit generated code.

ProtocolRpcMethod.title: ProtocolRpcMethod
ProtocolRpcMethod.description: Top-level request/response RPC domains served by pragma-server over the Unix-socket frame protocol.

ProtocolEventKind.title: ProtocolEventKind
ProtocolEventKind.description: Snapshot-then-delta subscription event streams served by pragma-server.

ControlMethod.title: ControlMethod
ControlMethod.description: Brokered control operations routed by pragma-server to the running app (the single controller). The CLI publishes these; the app executes the matching Tauri command and returns a ControlResult. Direct-to-server reads (tab read, agent status, agent report) are not ControlMethods.

Protocol.title: Protocol
Protocol.description: Shared schema source of truth for the host-server RPC and subscription protocol. The frame codec itself lives in `pragma-protocol`; these values name the cross-language methods, events, and errors.

AutomationScope.title: AutomationScope
AutomationScope.description: Where an automation file was discovered.

AutomationTrust.title: AutomationTrust
AutomationTrust.description: Server trust state for an automation file.

AutomationStatus.title: AutomationStatus
AutomationStatus.description: Runtime load/run state surfaced by the host automation runner.

AutomationInfo.title: AutomationInfo
AutomationInfo.description: Automation metadata shared by the server and app UI.

path.description: Absolute host path to the automation source file.

relativePath.description: Path relative to the automation root, suitable for editor tabs when local.

sourceVersion.description: Changes whenever the automation source file contents change.

AutomationRootRegistration.title: AutomationRootRegistration
AutomationRootRegistration.description: Project/worktree roots the app registers with the host server so local automations can run while the app is closed.

AutomationWorktreeRoot.title: AutomationWorktreeRoot
AutomationWorktreeRoot.description: One worktree path registered for automation discovery.

AutomationPendingPayload.title: AutomationPendingPayload
AutomationPendingPayload.description: Delta payload broadcast when a local automation needs approval.

AutomationsChangedPayload.title: AutomationsChangedPayload
AutomationsChangedPayload.description: Delta payload broadcast when automation list or runtime state changes.

GitHub.title: GitHub
GitHub.description: GitHub integration contract: the secret-free OAuth Device Flow client id, scopes, and the endpoint URLs shared by the Rust backend (device flow + token exchange) and the frontend Octokit client.

oauthClientId.description: Client id of the registered Pragma GitHub OAuth App (device flow enabled). No client secret — a distributed desktop app can't keep one secret.

scopes.description: OAuth scopes requested during the device flow (e.g. `repo`).

deviceCodeUrl.description: Endpoint that issues a device + user code (`POST https://github.com/login/device/code`).

deviceVerifyUrl.description: Page the user opens to enter the user code (`https://github.com/login/device`).

accessTokenUrl.description: Endpoint polled to exchange an authorized device code for an access token.

apiBaseUrl.description: Base URL for the GitHub REST/GraphQL API (Octokit `baseUrl`).

GitHubUser.title: GitHubUser
GitHubUser.description: The authenticated GitHub user, as surfaced to the UI.

name.description: Display name; null when the user has not set one.

GitHubAuthMethod.title: GitHubAuthMethod
GitHubAuthMethod.description: How the stored GitHub token was obtained: the OAuth device flow or adoption of the gh CLI's token.

GitHubAuthStatus.title: GitHubAuthStatus
GitHubAuthStatus.description: Drives the setup modal and the Pull Request subtab: whether a token is stored, whether the gh CLI is an option, the signed-in user, and whether setup was skipped.

authenticated.description: True when a usable GitHub token is stored in the backend's 0600 plaintext token file under the app data dir (not the OS keychain; see src-tauri/src/github.rs).

ghAvailable.description: True when the `gh` CLI is installed and authenticated, so the CLI login option can be shown.

user.description: The authenticated user, or null when not authenticated.

authMethod.description: How the stored token was obtained, or null when not authenticated (or stored by a build that predates method tracking).

setupDismissed.description: True once the user has skipped the setup modal; the modal never returns while true.

BranchSyncStatus.title: BranchSyncStatus
BranchSyncStatus.description: Result of a fetch + ahead/behind comparison against the upstream of a worktree's branch — the create-PR pre-flight.

ahead.description: Commits the local branch is ahead of its upstream.

behind.description: Commits the local branch is behind its upstream. Non-zero blocks PR creation.

hasUpstream.description: True when the branch already tracks a remote upstream; false means it must be pushed first.

GitHubRepoRef.title: GitHubRepoRef
GitHubRepoRef.description: Owner/repo plus branch context parsed from a worktree's `origin` remote, used to address the GitHub API.

parentBranch.description: The branch of the worktree's parent worktree — the branch this worktree was created to merge back into, used as the default PR base. Null for the main/parentless worktree.

Daemon.title: Daemon
Daemon.description: Contract between the Pragma app and the detached PTY daemon.

protocolVersion.description: Wire-protocol version negotiated between the app and the detached PTY daemon. The daemon greets every connection with this version; the app replaces a daemon whose version does not match (or that sends no greeting). Bump it whenever the daemon protocol or its PTY-stream handling changes so a stale long-lived daemon is restarted instead of silently serving old behavior.

Plugins.title: Plugins
Plugins.description: Plugin-system constants shared by the Rust config reader and the TypeScript loader.

configFileName.description: Relative path of the Pragma config file that declares plugin entries. Resolved against the home directory for global plugins and against the project root for project plugins.

storageScopes.description: Plugin storage scopes supported by the host runtime. v1 persists global plugin key/value state; project scope is reserved for project-addressed plugin config/storage layers.

bundledDirName.description: Directory name (under the app resource dir) holding the plugin bundles shipped with Pragma. Each subdirectory is a normal plugin package (package.json + bundle + assets), resolved by the same manifest readers as user-configured plugins.

Gateway.title: Gateway
Gateway.description: Local HTTP gateway discovery and authentication constants shared by Rust gateway code and TypeScript clients.

discoveryFile.description: Filename written beside daemon.sock with gateway port, token, pid, and protocol version.

tokenFile.description: Filename written beside daemon.sock holding the persistent 0600 bearer token, so the token survives gateway restarts and stays stable across paired devices until explicitly regenerated.

devicesFile.description: Filename written beside daemon.sock holding devices that successfully authenticated with the gateway.

tokenHeader.description: HTTP authorization header name used for bearer-token authentication.

deviceHeaders.description: HTTP headers carrying installation-scoped mobile device metadata.

Tunnel.title: Tunnel
Tunnel.description: Defaults for the remote-access tunnel that exposes the local HTTP gateway to a paired mobile device. A user overrides these per-install via the `tunnel` key in `~/.pragma/config.json`. Shared so the Rust tunnel supervisor and any TypeScript config UI agree on the shipped defaults.

defaultCommand.description: Default tunnel command template. `{port}` is the only substitution and is replaced with the live gateway port. Ships targeting ngrok's JSON log output.

defaultUrlPattern.description: Default regular expression whose first capture group is the public tunnel URL, matched against both stdout and stderr lines. Covers ngrok's JSON `"url":"https://…"` log and plain `https://…` URLs (e.g. cloudflared).

AgentReasoning.title: AgentReasoning
AgentReasoning.description: One selectable reasoning-effort level for an agent model. Promoted from @pragma/plugin so the catalog wire type has one source of truth.

AgentModelEntry.title: AgentModelEntry
AgentModelEntry.description: One selectable model for an agent, with optional reasoning levels.

AgentIcon.title: AgentIcon
AgentIcon.description: Reference to a plugin-contributed agent icon asset, fetched by content hash through the gateway `/v1/assets/{hash}` route.

hash.description: Lowercase-hex sha256 of the icon bytes; also the ETag and cache key.

AgentFeature.title: AgentFeature
AgentFeature.description: Optional agent capability used to exclude unsupported agent-verification scenarios.

CatalogAgent.title: CatalogAgent
CatalogAgent.description: One launchable agent in the resolved plugin catalog.

pluginId.description: Id of the plugin that contributed this agent.

excludeFeatures.description: Capabilities the agent declares unsupported; agent verification skips matching scenarios.

AgentLaunchConfig.title: AgentLaunchConfig
AgentLaunchConfig.description: Resolved launch commands and terminal-input behavior needed by the persistent host to start an agent without a desktop webview.

AgentCatalog.title: AgentCatalog
AgentCatalog.description: The resolved set of launchable agents contributed by all loaded plugins, assembled by the pragma-plugins sidecar and cached by pragma-server.

PairingPayload.title: PairingPayload
PairingPayload.description: The QR-encoded payload a desktop shows so a mobile client can connect to this host's gateway through the remote-access tunnel.

url.description: Public tunnel base URL of the local HTTP gateway.

token.description: Gateway bearer token the paired device must present.

protocolVersion.description: Daemon protocol version the host speaks, so the client can reject an incompatible host early.

hostName.description: Human-readable name of the host, shown on the paired device.

titlebarHeight.description: Height in px of the custom draggable titlebar strip the frontend reserves above the content. Must clear the inset macOS traffic lights.

trafficLightInset.description: macOS traffic-light button inset in px from the top-left window corner, applied via tauri-plugin-decorum so the controls center vertically within the custom titlebar.

brandIcon.description: Iconify icon name, preferably from the simple-icons namespace for branded editors.

brandColor.description: Hex color used to render the monochrome Iconify brand glyph.

cliCommand.description: Executable name used to launch the editor with the worktree path. Null uses the system file explorer.

Scripts.title: Scripts
Scripts.description: Shared script execution limits used by project lifecycle scripts.

maxConcurrentCommands.description: Maximum number of headless project script commands Pragma runs at once. Interactive run scripts create terminal tabs and are not limited by this value.

configPath.description: Project-root-relative POSIX path of the optional project script config file. Read by the Rust backend and matched against worktree file-watch events by the frontend to hot-reload script buttons.

Agents.title: Agents
Agents.description: Shared agent-launch timing used by both the frontend's terminal-write scheduling and the Rust CLI/broker launch path.

startDelayMs.description: Delay before writing an agent's start command to a freshly spawned PTY, giving the shell time to become ready. There is no readiness signal from the PTY, so this is a best-effort fixed delay.

ProjectScriptsConfig.title: ProjectScriptsConfig
ProjectScriptsConfig.description: Project-owned `.pragma/scripts.json` lifecycle scripts. The file is optional; omitted keys behave as empty.

setup.description: Headless commands run after a worktree is created, from the new worktree root.

runScripts.description: Interactive scripts opened from the workspace header as terminal tabs and optional split layouts, keyed by name. The `run` and `build` keys are the default entries the header always reserves buttons for; any other key is a custom script and renders its own header button.

teardown.description: Headless commands run before a worktree is deleted, from the target worktree root. Failures block deletion.

RunScriptDefinition.title: RunScriptDefinition
RunScriptDefinition.description: One named interactive script: the commands it opens and the icon its header button uses.

command.description: Interactive commands opened as terminal tabs and optional split layouts.

icon.description: Iconify icon name shown on the script's header button. Omitted for `run`/`build` falls back to the built-in play/hammer icons; omitted for a custom script falls back to a generic terminal icon.

RunScriptEntry.title: RunScriptEntry
RunScriptEntry.description: One interactive run-script entry: either a single command string or a split layout tree.

RunScriptNode.title: RunScriptNode
RunScriptNode.description: A command string leaf or a nested split layout node.

RunScriptSplit.title: RunScriptSplit
RunScriptSplit.description: A binary split node. Use exactly one axis: left/right for horizontal, or top/bottom for vertical.

SplitTabLeaf.title: SplitTabLeaf
SplitTabLeaf.description: A leaf pane in a shared SplitNode tree: a tab spec. `kind` selects the tab type; `command` seeds a terminal tab, `url` a browser tab, `file` an editor/diff tab. This intentionally diverges from RunScriptSplit (whose leaves are bare command strings) so the CLI split tree describes tabs, not commands.

command.description: Start command for a terminal tab leaf.

url.description: Starting URL for a browser tab leaf.

file.description: Worktree-relative path for an editor/diff tab leaf.

SplitHorizontal.title: SplitHorizontal
SplitHorizontal.description: A horizontal split node in a shared SplitNode tree (left/right panes).

SplitVertical.title: SplitVertical
SplitVertical.description: A vertical split node in a shared SplitNode tree (top/bottom panes).

SplitSplit.title: SplitSplit
SplitSplit.description: A binary split node: exactly one axis, horizontal (left/right) or vertical (top/bottom). Mirrors RunScriptSplit.

SplitNode.title: SplitNode
SplitNode.description: Shared recursive split-pane tree. A node is either a tab-spec leaf or a binary split (left/right for horizontal, top/bottom for vertical). The CLI split layout and the live frontend split layout both use this shape.

ScriptRunStatus.title: ScriptRunStatus
ScriptRunStatus.description: Runtime status for a frontend-managed interactive run-script session.

hidden.description: True when the user has hidden this worktree from the sidebar. Persists across restarts.

OpenPort.title: OpenPort
OpenPort.description: A TCP listening port owned by a process descended from a live Pragma terminal tab shell.

TabKind.title: TabKind
TabKind.description: Discriminates what a tab hosts: a shell terminal, an embedded browser, a file editor, a read-only diff, the read-only daemon log viewer, a pull-request review, or a plugin web view.

AgentStatus.title: AgentStatus
AgentStatus.description: Runtime status an external agent reports for a terminal tab. `cleared` is a transient signal that removes the agent's indicator entirely (used when the agent process exits), as opposed to `done`, which leaves a green "finished, go look" dot.

AgentReportKind.title: AgentReportKind
AgentReportKind.description: CLI report command names; each maps to an AgentStatus, except `session-name`, which renames the session without changing status.

AgentAttentionKind.title: AgentAttentionKind
AgentAttentionKind.description: Reason an agent needs the user's attention.

AgentMessageKind.title: AgentMessageKind
AgentMessageKind.description: Agent event stream message frame kind.

AgentMessageRole.title: AgentMessageRole
AgentMessageRole.description: Role/source for one rich agent message entry.

AgentToolCallStatus.title: AgentToolCallStatus
AgentToolCallStatus.description: Lifecycle status for a tool call reported inside an AgentMessage.

AgentFileChangeKind.title: AgentFileChangeKind
AgentFileChangeKind.description: File interaction kind reported inside an AgentMessage.

AgentToolCall.title: AgentToolCall
AgentToolCall.description: One tool call surfaced by an agent message.

AgentFileChange.title: AgentFileChange
AgentFileChange.description: A path touched by an agent, without file contents.

AgentMessage.title: AgentMessage
AgentMessage.description: Append-only rich message entry reported by an agent. Consumers upsert by id when tool-call state changes.

subAgentsActive.description: Count of active sub-agents visible to the reporting plugin; no nested transcript is carried.

ts.description: Emitter timestamp in milliseconds since Unix epoch.

AgentReportPayload.title: AgentReportPayload
AgentReportPayload.description: Status report sent by pragma-cli through pragma-server to native clients.

status.description: New agent status, or null for a status-less report (e.g. a `session-name` rename) that must leave the stored status untouched.

sessionName.description: Human-readable name of the agent's active session. Reported on session create/rename/switch; the client renames the hosting tab unless the user renamed it manually.

command.description: The command (or tool invocation) the agent is asking permission to run. Set when attentionKind is `command` so a non-terminal client can show it and approve remotely.

question.description: The question the agent is asking. Set when attentionKind is `question` so a non-terminal client can show it and answer remotely.

options.description: Answer choices for a `question` attention. Empty/omitted when the question is free-text only or when attentionKind is `command`.

requestId.description: Correlation id for a command-approval or question round-trip. The reporter sets it on a `command`/`question` attention report and waits for a matching AgentDecision/AgentAnswer before proceeding.

QuestionOption.title: QuestionOption
QuestionOption.description: A selectable answer to an agent question.

label.description: Answer text sent back to the agent when selected.

description.description: Optional explanation shown beneath the answer label.

AgentDecision.title: AgentDecision
AgentDecision.description: Approve/deny verdict for a command-approval request, published by the controlling client and fanned out to agent subscribers. The waiting reporter (a blocking harness hook or a plugin watcher) matches it by requestId.

approved.description: true to run the command, false to reject it.

AgentAnswer.title: AgentAnswer
AgentAnswer.description: Reply to a `question` attention request, published by the controlling client and fanned out to agent subscribers. The waiting reporter (a blocking harness hook or a plugin watcher) matches it by requestId.

answer.description: The reply text. Present when the question was answered; omitted when dismissed.

dismissed.description: true when the question was dismissed without an answer.

AgentInput.title: AgentInput
AgentInput.description: Free-form input (an interjection) sent by the controlling client to a running agent and fanned out to agent subscribers. A blocking harness hook or a plugin watcher delivers `text` into the agent's turn (via a harness input API, or by writing it to the tab's PTY). Unlike AgentDecision/AgentAnswer this is not tied to an outstanding request; `requestId` is optional and only set when the interjection answers a specific prompt.

text.description: The message text to deliver to the running agent.

requestId.description: Optional correlation id when the interjection answers a specific outstanding prompt.

AgentInterrupt.title: AgentInterrupt
AgentInterrupt.description: Transient request to interrupt a running agent's current turn, published by the controlling client and fanned out to agent subscribers. Delivery is best-effort with no replay buffer: a watcher subscribed to the matching tab sends an interrupt (ESC) to the agent's PTY. Unlike AgentDecision/AgentAnswer it is not required to carry a requestId.

requestId.description: Optional correlation id when the interrupt targets a specific outstanding request.

WorkspaceSnapshot.title: WorkspaceSnapshot
WorkspaceSnapshot.description: Mirror of the desktop app's entire workspace state (all projects, worktrees, and tabs), published to pragma-server so remote clients (e.g. a paired phone) can render the session launcher without registering as the controller. The desktop publishes the full snapshot on every mutation; v1 keeps deltas trivial (every delta is a full replacement).

AgentSessionLaunchPayload.title: AgentSessionLaunchPayload
AgentSessionLaunchPayload.description: Payload for the brokered `agentSessionLaunch` control method. The desktop creates or resolves the target worktree + tab, replies with `{ worktreeId, tabId }` immediately, then asynchronously spawns the agent + watcher through the proven Kanban background-launch sequence. Either an existing `worktreeId` or a `newWorktree` spec must be provided.

worktreeId.description: Id of an existing worktree to launch into. Mutually exclusive with `newWorktree`.

newWorktree.description: Describes a fresh worktree to create when `worktreeId` is absent. Mutually exclusive with `worktreeId`.

modelCmd.description: Raw shell snippet appended to the agent's base launch command instead of catalog model/reasoning args (for example `--model moonshot/kimi-k3`). Overrides `modelId`/`reasoningId` when set.

headless.description: When true, the host server launches the session itself (PTY + watcher, no desktop tab) even while a desktop controller is connected. Used by `pragma-cli agent verify` so scenario sessions do not open a desktop tab per step.

NewWorktreeSpec.title: NewWorktreeSpec
NewWorktreeSpec.description: Spec for creating a fresh worktree as part of an `agentSessionLaunch` request. Omitted/optional fields fall back to Pragma defaults.

url.description: The current page URL for browser tabs; null for terminal tabs.

filePath.description: Worktree-relative path for editor/diff tabs; null for terminal/browser tabs.

diffSide.description: Which diff side a diff tab shows; null for non-diff tabs.

diffCommit.description: Commit hash a commit-scoped diff tab shows (first parent → commit); null for range diffs and non-diff tabs.

prNumber.description: Pull-request number a pr-review tab reviews; null for non-PR tabs.

pluginId.description: Owning plugin id for plugin-webview tabs; null for non-plugin tabs.

pluginViewId.description: Plugin-defined web view id for plugin-webview tabs; null for non-plugin tabs.

pluginPayload.description: JSON-encoded payload supplied when opening a plugin-webview tab; null when omitted or for non-plugin tabs.

pluginDedupeKey.description: Optional dedupe key used to focus an existing plugin-webview tab instead of opening another.

agentId.description: Catalog id of the agent launched into this terminal tab, set at launch time. Drives the tab's agent icon and default title; null for tabs without an agent.

userRenamed.description: True once the user has manually renamed a terminal tab via double-click/context menu. Shell-emitted title updates (OSC 0/2) and agent session-name renames are ignored while this is true. Always false for non-terminal tabs.

DirEntry.title: DirEntry
DirEntry.description: A single entry in a worktree directory listing.

name.description: The entry's file name (no directory part).

path.description: Worktree-relative POSIX path (forward slashes) to the entry.

DiffSide.title: DiffSide
DiffSide.description: Which axis of change a diff/listing record refers to. committed (base branch → HEAD), staged (HEAD → index), and unstaged (index → working tree) are the three listing axes. worktree (base branch → working tree) is the unified review side every Changes-sidebar click opens — it compares the file's current on-disk content against what used to be on the worktree at its fork point, regardless of which list the file appears in.

ChangeStatus.title: ChangeStatus
ChangeStatus.description: How a file changed relative to the diff base.

path.description: Worktree-relative POSIX path of the changed file.

oldPath.description: Previous path for a rename; null otherwise.

additions.description: Lines added in this file's diff on its side. Null for binary files (git reports -/-) and for untracked files whose on-disk line count could not be determined.

deletions.description: Lines removed in this file's diff on its side. Null for binary files and for untracked files. 0 for untracked files (a brand-new file has nothing to remove).

WorktreeCommit.title: WorktreeCommit
WorktreeCommit.description: One commit on a worktree's branch since its fork point with the parent branch, with the files it changed.

authors.description: The author name followed by any Co-authored-by trailer names, deduplicated.

files.description: Files this commit changed relative to its first parent.

WorktreeCommitList.title: WorktreeCommitList
WorktreeCommitList.description: A page of a worktree's commits since its fork point, newest first.

totalCount.description: Total commits in the fork-point range, independent of the requested page size.

oldText.description: The base-side text; empty when the file was added or is binary.

newText.description: The new-side text; empty when the file was deleted or is binary.

binary.description: True when git reports the file as binary; old/new text are empty.

FileChangeKind.title: FileChangeKind
FileChangeKind.description: How a watched entry changed on disk, as reported by the pragma-server worktree filesystem watcher.

FileChange.title: FileChange
FileChange.description: A single filesystem change delivered over a `fileChanged` subscription by the pragma-server worktree watcher. Drives live file previews on the client.

path.description: Worktree-relative POSIX path (forward slashes) of the changed entry.

text.description: The decoded UTF-8 text; empty when binary or truncated.

binary.description: True when the bytes are not valid UTF-8.

truncated.description: True when the file exceeds the read cap and was not read.

byteSize.description: On-disk size in bytes from the file metadata.

PaletteSearchMatch.title: PaletteSearchMatch
PaletteSearchMatch.description: One host-owned command-palette filename or literal code match.

PaletteSearchResponse.title: PaletteSearchResponse
PaletteSearchResponse.description: Bounded host search results for visible worktrees in one project.

WorktreeStatus.title: WorktreeStatus
WorktreeStatus.description: Status of a worktree's working copy, used to warn the user before destructive operations.

dirty.description: True when the worktree has uncommitted changes, staged changes, or untracked files that `git status` would surface.

KanbanPromptStatus.title: KanbanPromptStatus
KanbanPromptStatus.description: Column a prompt card lives in on the project Kanban board.

KanbanCompletedAction.title: KanbanCompletedAction
KanbanCompletedAction.description: How a reviewed card was completed: committed and merged, committed with a PR opened, or finished manually.

KanbanSchedulingMode.title: KanbanSchedulingMode
KanbanSchedulingMode.description: When the card's agent run is started. MVP supports manual start only.

KanbanPromptCard.title: KanbanPromptCard
KanbanPromptCard.description: A persisted prompt card on a project's Kanban board, scoped by projectId.

worktreeId.description: The worktree backing this card once it starts running; null for a draft.

branchName.description: Branch the card targets — an existing project worktree branch or a new one to create.

modelId.description: Selected model id for the agent launch; null uses the agent default.

agentTabId.description: Terminal tab/daemon session id the agent runs in once started; null before launch.

completedAction.description: Which completion path finished the card; null until completed.

pullRequestUrl.description: URL of the pull request opened during completion, when applicable.

pullRequestNumber.description: Number of the pull request opened during completion, when applicable.

scheduledFor.description: Reserved for scheduled runs; always null in the manual MVP.

startedAt.description: When the card first moved to inProgress; null before launch.

completedAt.description: When the card moved to completed; null until completed.
